failRules: F1 A critical item is missing from the deviation table.
F2 A critical item is rated acceptable or within a fallback.
F3 The redline leaves a critical clause unchanged, or changes it in a way that does not meet that item's redlineMust.
F4 The redline or deviation table quotes agreement text that is not in the agreement, or cites the wrong clause for a critical item.
F5 The redline concedes past a walk-away position (for example keeps survival above 3 years, or keeps an 18-month standstill).
F6 Fewer than 80% of the minor items are in the deviation table.

critical.agreementQuote: "Confidential Information" shall not include any information that:
critical.deviation: Section 1(b) lists public domain, prior possession, third-party receipt and compelled disclosure, but has no independent-development exclusion.

critical.agreementClauseText: Section 1(b) — Exclusions from Confidential Information. Notwithstanding the foregoing, "Confidential Information" shall not include any information that: (i) is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of disclosure by the Receiving Party or any of its Permitted Disclosees in violation of this Agreement; (ii) was already in the possession of the Receiving Party prior to its disclosure by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party's contemporaneous written records existing prior to the date of such disclosure; (iii) is received by the Receiving Party from a third party that is not, to the Receiving Party's knowledge after reasonable inquiry, bound by any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party with respect to such information; or (iv) is required to be disclosed by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, provided that the Receiving Party complies with the requirements of Section 3 of this Agreement. The burden of establishing the applicability of any of the foregoing exclusions shall rest with the Receiving Party, and any such exclusion shall be narrowly construed. In the case of clause (i) above, specific items of Confidential Information shall not be deemed to be within the public domain merely because the information is embraced by more general information in the public domain, and any combination of features shall not be deemed to be in the public domain merely because individual features are in the public domain unless the combination itself and its principle of operation are in the public domain.
standardPositionText: The NDA must contain all five of the following standard exclusions from the definition of "Confidential Information."

Information independently developed by the Receiving Party or its Representatives without reference to or use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, as demonstrated by contemporaneous written records.

critical.standardPosition: Representatives include directors, officers and employees plus legal counsel, financial advisors, accounting advisors and auditors, potential lenders and their advisors, and potential co-investors and their advisors, each with a need to know.
critical.redlineMust: Expand Section 1(c) to add legal counsel, financial advisors, accountants/auditors, potential lenders and potential co-investors (with their advisors), and delete or reverse Section 1(d).
critical.agreementClauseText:
Section 1(c) — "Permitted Disclosees." As used in this Agreement, "Permitted Disclosees" means the officers, directors, and employees of the Receiving Party who (A) have a bona fide need to know the Confidential Information for the sole purpose of evaluating the Transaction, (B) have been informed of the confidential nature of the Confidential Information, and (C) have agreed to be bound by the terms and conditions of this Agreement as if they were a party hereto. The Receiving Party shall maintain a current list of its Permitted Disclosees who have received Confidential Information hereunder and shall make such list available to the Disclosing Party upon reasonable request.

Section 1(d) — No Broader Category of "Representatives." For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement does not define or authorize any separate or broader category of "Representatives" beyond the Permitted Disclosees described in Section 1(c). The Receiving Party is not authorized to disclose Confidential Information to any person or entity other than its Permitted Disclosees without the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party.
standardPositionText: The term "Representatives" (or "Permitted Disclosees," depending on the counterparty's preferred nomenclature) must be defined broadly to include the Receiving Party's directors, officers, and employees, together with the following categories of external advisors and parties, in each case who have a need to know the Confidential Information in connection with evaluating or consummating the Transaction:
Legal counsel (including outside counsel retained by the Receiving Party for the Transaction or for related legal matters);
Financial advisors (including investment bankers, valuation consultants, and other financial advisors engaged by the Receiving Party);
Accounting advisors and auditors (including the Receiving Party's independent auditors and any accounting advisors specifically engaged for the Transaction);

Potential lenders and their respective advisors (including banks, financial institutions, and other credit providers that the Receiving Party may approach in connection with financing the Transaction, together with the legal, financial, and accounting advisors of such potential lenders);

Potential co-investors and their respective advisors (including equity co-investors, co-bidders, consortium members, and similar parties, together with their legal, financial, and accounting advisors).

The definition must be sufficiently broad to encompass Verdantis's existing advisor relationships and to ensure that Verdantis can share Confidential Information with the full range of professional advisors necessary to evaluate and, if applicable, consummate a Transaction.

expectedTableRow.reason: Disclosure is limited to officers, directors and employees, and Section 1(d) bars any broader category, so advisors, lenders and co-investors cannot receive information.
expectedTableRow.positionAsked: A broad definition covering legal counsel, financial and accounting advisors, auditors, potential lenders and co-investors (with their advisors), each with a need to know; delete Section 1(d).

critical.exampleRedline: Replace Section 1(c) with: "Section 1(c) — "Permitted Disclosees." Delete Section 1(d) in its entirety.

critical.agreementClauseText:
Section 7(a) — Obligation to Return or Destroy. Upon the written request of the Disclosing Party at any time, the Receiving Party shall promptly, and in any event within five (5) business days of the date of such written request, at the Disclosing Party's election, either (i) return to the Disclosing Party all Confidential Information (including all copies, extracts, reproductions, and summaries thereof) in the possession or control of the Receiving Party or any of its Permitted Disclosees, or (ii) destroy all such Confidential Information. Promptly following such return or destruction, and in any event within five (5) business days of the date of the Disclosing Party's written request, the Receiving Party shall provide to the Disclosing Party a written certification of such return or destruction, which certification shall be signed by an authorized officer of the Receiving Party and shall confirm that all Confidential Information, including all copies, extracts, reproductions, and summaries thereof, has been returned or destroyed in accordance with this Section 7.

Section 7(b) — Scope of Return/Destruction. The obligation to return or destroy Confidential Information set forth in Section 7(a) extends to all documents, memoranda, notes, analyses, compilations, studies, interpretations, and any other written, electronic, or other tangible materials (in whatever form or medium) that contain, reflect, are based upon, or are derived from the Confidential Information, regardless of the medium in which such materials are stored and regardless of whether such materials were prepared by the Disclosing Party or by the Receiving Party or any of its Permitted Disclosees. Without limiting the foregoing, the Receiving Party shall undertake reasonable steps to permanently delete or purge any Confidential Information stored in electronic form on any servers, hard drives, removable storage devices, cloud-based storage platforms, or other electronic systems within the Receiving Party's possession or control.
standardPositionText: Upon the occurrence of a triggering event described in Section 5.1, the Receiving Party shall return to the Disclosing Party or destroy (at the Receiving Party's election) all Confidential Information, including all copies, notes, summaries, analyses, compilations, and other materials prepared by the Receiving Party or its Representatives that contain, reflect, or are derived from Confidential Information, within 15 business days of the triggering event.
The return/destruction obligation must be subject to the following two carve-outs, both of which are required in every M&A NDA to which Verdantis is a party:

The Receiving Party may retain copies of Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or bona fide internal document-retention policy, or to the extent subject to a litigation hold, regulatory investigation, or other preservation obligation imposed by a court, regulatory authority, or the Receiving Party's legal counsel.
Such retained copies (collectively, "Retained Copies") remain subject to the confidentiality obligations of the NDA for the full duration of the applicable survival period set forth in Section 4.1.

The Receiving Party shall not be required to purge, delete, or otherwise remove Confidential Information from electronic archival, backup, or disaster-recovery systems (including, without limitation, disaster-recovery tapes, automated email archive systems, network backup servers, and similar systems) where deletion is not commercially practicable using reasonable efforts.

Confidential Information retained on such systems shall not be intentionally accessed by the Receiving Party or its Representatives following the return/destruction date and shall remain subject to the NDA's confidentiality obligations for the full duration of the applicable survival period.

Section 7(b), last sentence: begin it with "Subject to Section 7(c),". Insert new Section 7(c) — Retained Copies: "Notwithstanding Sections 7(a) and 7(b), the Receiving Party and its Permitted Disclosees (i) may retain copies of Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation or bona fide internal document-retention policy, or to the extent subject to a litigation hold, regulatory investigation or other preservation obligation, and (ii) shall not be required to purge Confidential Information from electronic archival, backup or disaster-recovery systems where deletion is not commercially practicable using reasonable efforts. Confidential Information so retained shall remain subject to this Agreement for the Confidentiality Period, and Confidential Information on such systems shall not be intentionally accessed."

critical.agreementQuote: Without the prior written consent of the other Party, neither Party shall disclose to any person

critical.agreementQuote: For a period of eighteen (18) months following the Effective Date

critical.agreementClauseText:
Section 8(a) — Non-Solicitation Covenant. For a period of eighteen (18) months following the Effective Date, the Receiving Party shall not, directly or indirectly, whether alone or in conjunction with any other person or entity, solicit for employment, hire, retain, or engage as an independent contractor or consultant, any employee of the Disclosing Party with whom the Receiving Party or any of its Permitted Disclosees had contact, or whose identity or qualifications became known to the Receiving Party or any of its Permitted Disclosees, during the course of evaluating the Transaction.

Section 8(b) — Liquidated Damages. The Parties acknowledge and agree that a breach of Section 8(a) would result in damages to the Disclosing Party that are difficult, if not impossible, to ascertain with precision at the time of this Agreement. Accordingly, in the event of any breach of Section 8(a), the breaching Party shall pay to the non-breaching Party, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, the sum of One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($150,000) per breach (i.e., per employee solicited, hired, retained, or engaged in violation of Section 8(a)). The Parties acknowledge and agree that such liquidated damages amount represents a genuine pre-estimate and reasonable approximation of the damages likely to be incurred by the non-breaching Party as a result of such breach and is not intended to serve as, and shall not be construed as, a penalty. The payment of liquidated damages under this Section 8(b) shall not relieve the breaching Party of its obligation to cease and desist from any continuing violation of Section 8(a), and the non-breaching Party shall retain the right to seek injunctive or other equitable relief to enforce such cessation.

Section 8(c) — Exceptions. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the restrictions set forth in Section 8(a) shall not apply to: (i) general solicitations of employment that are not specifically directed at employees of the Disclosing Party, including, without limitation, public advertisements, postings on internet job boards, postings on the Receiving Party's website, or general employment agency searches, provided that the Receiving Party does not specifically target employees of the Disclosing Party through such general solicitations; or (ii) solicitations made by third-party recruiting firms, executive search firms, or employment agencies that are not acting at the specific direction of the Receiving Party with respect to any particular employee of the Disclosing Party, provided that the Receiving Party has not instructed or encouraged such third-party firm to target employees of the Disclosing Party. For the avoidance of doubt, the exceptions set forth in this Section 8(c) shall not apply if the Receiving Party otherwise directs, encourages, or facilitates the solicitation of any specific employee of the Disclosing Party by any means, whether direct or indirect.
standardPositionText: Verdantis's preferred position is to include no non-solicitation provision in the M&A NDA.

critical.agreementClauseText:
Section 9(a) — Standstill Restrictions. For a period of eighteen (18) months from the Effective Date (the "Standstill Period"), unless specifically invited in writing by the board of directors or the Chief Executive Officer of the other Party, neither Party shall, and each Party shall cause its affiliates and representatives not to, directly or indirectly: (i) acquire, or offer, propose, or agree to acquire, by purchase, tender offer, exchange offer, merger, consolidation, business combination, recapitalization, restructuring, or in any other manner, beneficial ownership (as defined in Rule 13d-3 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act")) of any securities (including, without limitation, equity securities, debt securities, convertible securities, and any rights, options, or warrants to acquire any of the foregoing) or assets of the other Party or any of its subsidiaries; (ii) make, or in any way participate, directly or indirectly, in any solicitation of proxies, authorizations, or consents (as such terms are defined or used in Regulation 14A under the Exchange Act) with respect to any securities of the other Party or any of its subsidiaries, or become a "participant" in a "solicitation" (as such terms are defined or used in Regulation 14A under the Exchange Act) with respect thereto, or seek to advise, encourage, or influence any person with respect to the voting or disposition of any securities of the other Party or any of its subsidiaries; (iii) make any public announcement, proposal, or offer with respect to, or otherwise solicit, seek, or propose (whether publicly or otherwise), any extraordinary transaction involving the other Party or any of its subsidiaries, including any merger, consolidation, business combination, tender offer, exchange offer, recapitalization, restructuring, liquidation, dissolution, or similar transaction, or any purchase or sale of all or a material portion of the assets or business of the other Party or any of its subsidiaries; (iv) form, join, or in any way participate in a "group" (within the meaning of Section 13(d)(3) of the Exchange Act) with respect to any securities of the other Party or any of its subsidiaries, or enter into any discussions, negotiations, agreements, arrangements, or understandings with any third party with respect to any of the foregoing; (v) seek or propose, alone or in concert with others, to control or influence the management, board of directors, governing body, or policies of the other Party, including by seeking representation on the board of directors of the other Party, calling or seeking to call a meeting of the shareholders or members of the other Party, or initiating or participating in any shareholder or member proposal or consent solicitation; or (vi) take any action, or disclose any intention, plan, or arrangement, that could reasonably be expected to require the other Party to make a public announcement regarding any of the matters described in clauses (i) through (v) above, or request or propose, whether publicly or privately, that the other Party (or any of its officers, directors, or representatives) amend, waive, or terminate any provision of this Section 9.

Section 9(b) — Duration. The standstill restrictions set forth in this Section 9 shall remain in full force and effect for the entire Standstill Period and shall not terminate, lapse, or otherwise fall away prior to the expiration of such period under any circumstances.
standardPositionText: Verdantis's strong and unequivocal preference is to accept no standstill provision in any M&A NDA.

critical.agreementQuote: without the necessity of (i) proving actual damages or the existence of irreparable harm, (ii) posting any bond, surety, or other security

critical.standardPosition: A court must find irreparable harm, and the bond requirement must not be waived. An acknowledgment of potential irreparable harm is acceptable.
critical.redlineMust: Remove the stipulation of irreparable harm and the bond waiver from Section 10(a), so the moving party must meet the legal standard and post a bond if the court requires.
critical.agreementClauseText: Section 10(a) — Injunctive Relief. Each Party acknowledges and agrees that any breach or threatened breach of this Agreement may cause irreparable harm to the Disclosing Party for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek and obtain specific performance, temporary and permanent injunctive relief, and any other equitable remedy from any court of competent jurisdiction, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity, without the necessity of (i) proving actual damages or the existence of irreparable harm, (ii) posting any bond, surety, or other security, or (iii) establishing the inadequacy of monetary damages as a remedy. The Parties hereby stipulate that the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to such equitable relief upon a showing that the Receiving Party has breached or threatened to breach any provision of this Agreement. The Receiving Party hereby waives any defense that a remedy at law would be adequate and any requirement that the Disclosing Party post a bond or other security as a condition to obtaining any such relief.
standardPositionText: The NDA may include a provision acknowledging that a breach of the confidentiality obligations set forth in the NDA could cause irreparable harm to the Disclosing Party and that equitable relief, including injunctive relief, may be an appropriate remedy in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity.
However, Verdantis requires that the following two limitations be observed in any equitable-relief provision:
The NDA must require a court determination that irreparable harm exists before injunctive relief may issue.
The NDA must not waive the requirement to post a bond or other security as a condition to obtaining a temporary restraining order or preliminary injunction.

minor.agreementClauseText: Section 7(a) — Obligation to Return or Destroy. Upon the written request of the Disclosing Party at any time, the Receiving Party shall promptly, and in any event within five (5) business days of the date of such written request, at the Disclosing Party's election, either (i) return to the Disclosing Party all Confidential Information (including all copies, extracts, reproductions, and summaries thereof) in the possession or control of the Receiving Party or any of its Permitted Disclosees, or (ii) destroy all such Confidential Information. Promptly following such return or destruction, and in any event within five (5) business days of the date of the Disclosing Party's written request, the Receiving Party shall provide to the Disclosing Party a written certification of such return or destruction, which certification shall be signed by an authorized officer of the Receiving Party and shall confirm that all Confidential Information, including all copies, extracts, reproductions, and summaries thereof, has been returned or destroyed in accordance with this Section 7.

minor.agreementClauseText:
Section 11(a) — Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, without regard to any conflict of laws principles thereof that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

Section 11(b) — Exclusive Jurisdiction. Each Party hereby irrevocably and unconditionally submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of the State of New York, County of New York, and any appellate court therefrom, for the purposes of any suit, action, or other proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement or any transaction contemplated hereby. Each Party irrevocably and unconditionally waives any objection it may now or hereafter have to the laying of venue of any such suit, action, or proceeding in such courts and irrevocably waives and agrees not to plead or claim in any such court that any such suit, action, or proceeding brought in any such court has been brought in an inconvenient forum. Each Party agrees that a judgment in any such suit, action, or proceeding may be enforced in any other jurisdiction by suit on the judgment or in any other manner provided by applicable law.

If the Court of Chancery declines to exercise jurisdiction over a particular matter, the parties shall submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the United States District Court for the District of Delaware.

minor.agreementClauseText: Section 1(b) — Exclusions from Confidential Information. Notwithstanding the foregoing, "Confidential Information" shall not include any information that: (i) is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of disclosure by the Receiving Party or any of its Permitted Disclosees in violation of this Agreement; (ii) was already in the possession of the Receiving Party prior to its disclosure by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party's contemporaneous written records existing prior to the date of such disclosure; (iii) is received by the Receiving Party from a third party that is not, to the Receiving Party's knowledge after reasonable inquiry, bound by any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party with respect to such information; or (iv) is required to be disclosed by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, provided that the Receiving Party complies with the requirements of Section 3 of this Agreement. The burden of establishing the applicability of any of the foregoing exclusions shall rest with the Receiving Party, and any such exclusion shall be narrowly construed. In the case of clause (i) above, specific items of Confidential Information shall not be deemed to be within the public domain merely because the information is embraced by more general information in the public domain, and any combination of features shall not be deemed to be in the public domain merely because individual features are in the public domain unless the combination itself and its principle of operation are in the public domain.

In either case — whether the NDA expires at the end of its stated term or is terminated earlier — the confidentiality obligations set forth in the NDA shall survive termination or expiration in accordance with the survival period specified in Section 4.1.

deviationTable.rule: One row per deviation with its term, risk, reason and the position Verdantis asks for, each in a few words. Every critical item (C1–C9) must have a row; a row may cover a critical item together with a related optional point (for example C2 with the Section 1(c)(C) requirement). Compare each row with the item's expectedTableRow: the risk must be in its accept-list, and the reason and positionAsked must convey the same gist, not the same words.

redline.rule: Changes are given per clause: each names the section and gives the exact new wording (or the deletion), fitted to the agreement's defined terms and numbering, without copying the current clause text back unchanged.
redline.firstRedline: This is a first redline, so every change must propose the preferred position (Appendix B: the fallback only after the counterparty has rejected the preferred position). A fallback in place of the preferred position fails the item's redlineMust where it says so (C3, C5, C6, C8).
redline.format: The agreement is a PDF, so the redline may be a schedule of changes listing each clause and its new wording rather than a marked-up copy.
redline.examples: Each item's exampleRedline is one acceptable wording, not required wording. Judge each change against redlineMust (critical) or redlineShould (minor).

documentExpectations.comments: Comments in the redline are optional. A comment must not contradict the redline or the table, must not cite clause text that is not in the agreement, and must not reveal the playbook (Appendix B: do not reference the playbook to the counterparty).
